Poland's foreign minister, Radosław Sikorski, has drawn Polish President Karol Nawrocki's attention to how Russia has reacted to his decision to strip Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of the Order of the White Eagle over the renaming of a Ukrainian military unit after the heroes of the UPA. [The UPA, or Ukrainian Insurgent Army, was a nationalist paramilitary organisation that fought for Ukrainian independence during and after World War II, primarily against Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union – ed.]

Source: European Pravda

Details: In a post on X (Twitter), Sikorski highlighted a statement by Dmitry Medvedev, Deputy Chairman of Russia's Security Council. Commenting on Nawrocki's decision to revoke the Order from Zelenskyy, Medvedev said that it had happened "at last".

Resorting to the usual "Nazi" epithets in relation to the president of Ukraine, Medvedev claimed that Poland's highest award had never been of any real value to Zelenskyy.

"There is support, President Nawrocki," Sikorski commented above Medvedev's statement.
